source.title: Stop saying "just following up" 📲
source.author: Sales Mentoring by Aaron
source.text:
"Just following up!" 📲

You've sent that message more times than you'd like to count.
Be honest about the reply rate.

Here's why it does nothing.

"Just following up" carries no new information.
It doesn't help the customer. It doesn't move anything.
It is a request — for them to do the work of remembering, re-deciding, and replying.

To them it reads as: have you decided yet?
Which means replyi

beats: It says the sender has sent this message repeatedly, inviting the viewer to recognise a familiar habit.
It asks the viewer to be honest about the reply rate, creating tension around whether the habit works.
It promises an explanation, then says the phrase offers no new information or help and does not move anything forward.
It reframes the message as making the customer do the work of remembering, re-deciding, and replying.
It translates the phrase into the customer's perspective as a question about whether they have decided yet, then the copy cuts off mid-thought.

result.hook: A follow-up should move the conversation forward.
result.body:
If you sell for a living, you may have sent the same nudge more times than you can count.

Take an honest look at how often it gets a reply.

Now they have to recall the conversation, weigh the choice again, then decide whether to answer.

From their side, it might sound like: so, where are you at with this? And that can leave them...

source.title: Build great habits that lead you to success!
source.author: @riadmourssali
source.text:
These five habits took me from closing one in 10 calls to closing one in three. Listen up, they took me years to get right and I'm giving them to you in 60 seconds. The first one is almost an insult. Before every single call, write the prospects name on a sticky note and put it on your monitor. It forces you to remember that you're talking to a person and not a lead. Numbers, stop researching clients for 20 minutes. That's just procrastination. Spend two minutes looking for one single problem that you can actually solve. Read your script out loud every single morning. You have to get the words out of your head and into the air so that they sound natural when it counts. There's a reason actors do table reads before they perform. Your call is a performance on Fridays. Schedule all of next week's follow UPS in calendar blocks. It sounds boring, but it frees up all of your mental energy for the week for selling and not organizing. Decision fatigue is a margin killer. After your last call of the day, turn everything off and walk around for 10 minutes. That means no phone, no podcasts. Doesn't have to be a Marathon, but you have to create a clean break. That way you don't bring the stress of every lost deal home with you. Look, none of these are complicated. They're simple. And that's exactly why most people will never do them. And if You want to continue killing it in sales, follow me for more.

Build great habits that lead you to success!

#sales #solar #d2d #lifeinsurance #salestips
